ideas.name: Beekeeping and the three sorts of bee

en.text: Beekeeping, or apiculture, is managing honeybees in hives for pollination and products: honey, wax, royal jelly, propolis and pollen. Bees are social insects. A colony has one queen that lays eggs, about 500 drones that mate with a young queen, and up to 40,000 workers that do all the work.

screens.after: Honey is food, is used in traditional medicine and brings income. Read about beekeeping.

screens.title: 3.5 Bee keeping
paras: Beekeeping (apiculture) is managing honeybees in hives.
It gives pollination, honey and other products.
Other products are wax, royal jelly, propolis and pollen.
Honey bees are social insects. They work together to survive.

notes.text: The book says a queen can lay 1,000 eggs a day; at peak season it can be more. Kept as printed.
Review Part I Q6 (drone is the father of the hive): left out: the book seems to expect False, but drones do father the brood. Replaced in practise by a question on the drone's job.
Activity 17 asks about health uses of bee products; the book does not give them, so only the named products are tested.
